thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: continuous-batcher growth detected in us-west-2 (pool: cont-batcher-1). Multiple nodes reporting CUDA OOM and container restarts. Avg latency ↑ 3x, tail latency exploding. Auto-escalation: high

maya: seeing it, ack. I'm on-call. bringing up logs now. @sanjay can you shadow?

sanjay: on it. pinged infra too. any immediate customer hits?

olivia: FYI support - ticket CP-1287 just reported ~10min of timeouts for embedding endpoints hitting that cluster. Customers impacted: two enterprise tenants (saturn, cedar).

maria: opened incident doc: https://redwood-internal/incident/1934567890 (adding customer names + contact).

maya: quick dump from one affected pod (cont-batcher-1-57c9):
```\n2026-03-15T04:02:11Z runtime ERROR: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 28.40 GiB already allocated; 1.85 GiB free; 3.50 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)\nBatcherQueue: queue_len=1240 inflight=98 avg_batch=64\nKERNEL: cudnn RUNTIME_ERROR at /workspace/cuda/conv.cu: line 142\nContainer exited with code 137\n```
maya: a few pods are OOM-killing the runtime process then kube restarting -> crashloop. batcher queue is continuously growing; looks like prefix cache miss pattern + new batching heuristic was applied in last rollout.

sanjay: 2 hypotheses: (A) new continuous-batching heuristic increases batch merge window causing very large batches that blow memory; (B) kernel-level CUDA regression on newer image.

derek: can we flip traffic to fallback model variant (smaller seq-len / quantized) while we triage?

maya: yes. I'll put a temporary routing rule to force small-variant. Executing:
```\n# pin to small-variant across route /v1/generate\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood/route/override \\\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \\\n  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"gpt-small-v2","duration":"15m","note":"mitigate OOMs"}'\n```
maya: applied override. starting to see latency drop on control plane metrics.

ops-bot: [action] Route override accepted by control-plane. changed 12 services.

olivia: customer update drafted, sending now: "We're aware of increased latency and are routing traffic to a lower-memory model variant while we investigate. We'll follow up with timeline." :white_check_mark:

sanjay: attempting live rollback of the batching heuristic config. current rollout id: rollout/cont-batch-v3 -> rolling back to cont-batch-v2.

maya: try also setting a hard cap on batch size to 128 as immediate patch:
```\n# runtime flag via config API\ncurl -X PATCH https://api.redwood/config/cont-batcher-1 \\\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \\\n  -d '{"max_batch_size":128,"batch_window_ms":10}'\n```

ops-bot: [action] Config patch queued, applying to nodes in pool cont-batcher-1 (strategy: rolling, parallelism=2).

maria: logging customer impact + risk level (high). Noted support contacts and started P1 Slack channel for SATURN team.

sanjay: patch landed to 4/6 nodes, observed immediate reduction in per-batch allocation. still seeing two hotspots that hit 28GB alloc. grabbing full oops trace.

maya: running `kubectl exec` into a hotspot pod to collect dmesg and nvidia-smi snapshots:
```\n$ kubectl exec -it cont-batcher-1-57c9 -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv\nmemory.used [MiB], memory.total [MiB]\n29124 MiB, 32510 MiB\n```

maya: also found a stack trace in /var/log/runner.log referencing `KVCache::apply_prefix_merge()` with huge input length. Looks consistent with merged requests exceeding expected sequence length.

derek: infra suggests cordon+drain of the two worst nodes to force traffic redistribution, then restart runtime containers after patch applied.

maya: cordoning node ip-10-0-7-12 now.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-1934567890. Severity=SEV-2. Pager escalations set.

olivia: customer update sent to Saturn (CRO) and Cedar (CS). both acknowledged; Saturn asked for ETA on full resolution.

sanjay: rollback of cont-batch-v3 completed. full rollback took ~8 minutes. metrics show reduction in avg batch size and memory pressure. still watching for residual OOMs.

maya: applying final mitigation: set runtime flag disable_continuous_merge=true and keep max_batch_size=128 while we cut a patch that caps aggregate tokens per-batch.

ops-bot: [action] runtime config updated on 6/6 nodes.

maria: documenting mitigation steps in incident doc and adding checklist for on-call playbook: revert-continuous-batcher, set-max-batch, route-to-variant, drain-nodes.

derek: can we add a temporary autoscale rule to spin up 3 extra nodes for cont-batcher-1 until tomorrow morning? that buys safety margin.

maya: approved. infra creating ec2 instances with GPU profiles. will monitor cost vs risk.

olivia: updated customers: "We're routing to fallback variants and have applied mitigations; we expect reduced errors within 15-30 minutes. We're preparing a post-incident report."

sanjay: follow-up items: 1) root-cause: batching heuristic allowed unbounded merge across prefixes, need regression test for max-merged-sequence; 2) add OOM circuit-breaker (drop too-large batches); 3) add alert for sustained queue growth (>300 in 5m).

maya: handing off primary incident owner to @sanjay for the 2-hr stabilization window. I'll remain available for questions.

sanjay: taking over. will coordinate postmortem. tagging @derek for infra follow-up, @maria for customer comms.

olivia: thanks team. reactions: :thumbsup: :coffee:

maria: marking incident as ongoing in tracker. last check: latency trending down to 1.2x baseline, OOMs reduced to single-digit across pool. will update when stabilized.

ops-bot: [status] pool cont-batcher-1: queue_len=72 avg_batch=40 OOM_events=3 (1h)
